base_retrieval.note: Task 3.5 selected dense-only retrieval; Task 3.6 selected no_rerank (reranking credibly regressed quality). CRAG grades confidence over this exact unreranked dense-only candidate pool.

score_source_decision: PROJECT_EXECUTION.md Task 3.7 names 'top-1 reranker score' as a candidate feature, but Task 3.6 selected no_rerank - there is no reranker score. Every feature is computed from the frozen Task 3.3 dense retrieval score (cosine similarity, higher=better) instead - a feature-source substitution forced by Task 3.6's own result, not a reopening of it.
population_decision: Every other Phase 3 task (3.1-3.6) evaluates ranking quality on the frozen 89-question DEV/evaluable-subset, which contains ONLY answerable questions - it has zero 'should refuse' examples and cannot calibrate or measure a refusal gate alone. CRAG's population is therefore two disjoint DEV subsets, neither newly invented: should_answer = the exact frozen 89-question scope (unchanged); should_refuse = every DEV question whose (category,subtype) is in src.eval.phase3_baseline.NOT_APPLICABLE_SHAPES (unanswerable/year_outside_window, adversarial/prompt_injection, adversarial/financial_advice, adversarial/off_scope) - a fixed classification already defined in Task 3.1, reused verbatim. Deliberately EXCLUDED: DEV questions that are retrieval-applicable but whose gold document is missing from the indexed corpus (the ~94% of DEV Task 3.1 excluded from the 89-question scope) - reusing that population here would silently reopen Task 3.1's own scope decision without review.

should_refuse_scope.note: Verified against the live full DEV set at plan time: 71+16+13+13 = 113 questions.

features.top1_score: dense retrieval score (cosine similarity) of the rank-1 candidate
features.top3_mean_score: mean dense retrieval score of the top-3 candidates
features.top1_top5_gap: top1_score - rank5_score (0.0 if fewer than 5 candidates)
features.candidate_count: candidates remaining after metadata pre-filtering (always 50 - Task 3.9's filter is disabled)

decision_rule: refuse iff top1_score < calibrated_threshold (src.crag.confidence.should_refuse) - single-feature gate; the other three features are recorded for diagnostic/future-task use but do not gate the decision in this round.
calibration_note: Deterministic, non-parametric sweep over every observed top1_score as a candidate threshold, maximizing true_refusal_rate - false_refusal_rate (Youden's J / balanced accuracy) - src.crag.confidence.calibrate_threshold_youden_j. Ties broken by the lowest candidate threshold (fewer false refusals). Calibrated and measured on the same should_answer/should_refuse population (DEV-only, no held-out split) - PROJECT_EXECUTION.md's own Task 3.7 instruction is 'Calibrate thresholds on DEV only', consistent with how every other frozen Phase 3 threshold (e.g. the practical-tie rules) was set with visibility into DEV behavior. Documented as a known optimistic-bias limitation, not hidden.
per_intent_thresholds: Not attempted in this round (single global threshold) - PROJECT_EXECUTION.md's 'prefer per-intent thresholds if score distributions differ' is deferred pending a first look at whether the four should_refuse shapes' score distributions actually differ materially; documented as a limitation, not silently skipped.
metric_definitions: true_refusal_rate/false_refusal_rate/missed_failure_rate via src.eval.metrics.aggregate_rate (Task 2.6, reused unmodified) over src.crag.confidence.classify_outcome() labels - never a new rate-computation implementation.
